Q: How much Linux knowledge is required before learning Red Hat OpenShift for production environments? A:

First of all I was a certified Red Hat Trainer with more than 5 years of experiences in Red Hat Trainings

  • What Linux skills are essential before learning OpenShift?

I recommend you to have basic Linux administration knowledge or experiences (Specially which covers in RHCSA at least). Thats the minimum req for follow this course (not must).

  • Should I learn container basics like Docker or Podman first?

Docker and Podman are containerisation platforms, so if you have any idea about any of containerisation tool, that would be great. Anyway in RHCSA this has been covered.

  • Is Kubernetes knowledge required before OpenShift?

It is not mandatory, since container knowledge is enough to start with OpenShift(something good to have)

  • What real-world skills are expected for production environments?

You may learn access control, networking, storage, scale in scale out, monitor, deployments, troubleshooting workloads and many more. OpenShift trianing covers cluster management and operations.

Q: How to restart a Docker Compose service if it stops producing stdout for 5 minutes? A:

Monitoring stdout with a Bash loop works, but it's not very idiomatic. A cleaner approach is to rely on Docker healthchecks and restart policies instead of parsing logs.

You can define a healthcheck that detects inactivity (for example, checking if a timestamp file hasn't been updated for 5 minutes):

services:
  uploader:
    image: your-image
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "test $(($(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y /tmp/last-output 2>/dev/null || echo 0))) -lt 300"]
      interval: 1m
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3

Then update the timestamp whenever your process produces output:

touch /tmp/last-output

If the container stops producing output, Docker marks it as unhealthy, and you can restart it automatically.

If you also want to respect normal exit codes, another clean option is:

while true; do
  docker compose up --abort-on-container-exit --exit-code-from uploader
  exit_code=$?

  [ "$exit_code" -eq 0 ] && break

  echo "Restarting due to inactivity..."
  sleep 5
done

This avoids fragile stdout parsing, respects exit code 0, and is easier to maintain.
